title: Week 4: The Big Freeze

theme.name: The Big Freeze
theme.text: Snow, ice and frozen pipes. Shops can barely open. Business slows a little every few cards.

cards.text: Mayor! The river's frozen solid! I want an ice rink! Skating! Ice hockey! Geese versus town! Open the river?

right.label: Yes. Open the rink.
right.reaction: Four hundred skaters by lunch. Gerald is skating. On his face. It works for him.

left.label: No. Too dangerous.
left.reaction: Coach is skating anyway. Alone. In a circle. Shouting encouragement at himself.

cards.text: Mayor, I've put spikes on my scooter. I want to drive it on the ice. Forty miles an hour. It's for science. Let me?

right.label: Yes. Go, Bev.
right.reaction: She did a lap in eleven seconds. Then a jump. Then another jump. Nobody asked for the jumps.

left.label: No. Skates only.
left.reaction: She's on skates. Somehow faster. She's lapping the geese.

cards.text: Mayor. Coach Dunk has been skating alone on the river for six hours. He's shouting 'GOOD HUSTLE' at a duck. Bring him in?

right.label: Yes. Bring him in.
right.reaction: We brought him in. He's wrapped in a blanket. He's given the blanket a team talk.

left.label: No. Let him skate.
left.reaction: The duck has joined him. They're a team now. The duck's very fast.

cards.text: HONK. (Gerald would like an ice hockey match. Geese against the town. Tonight. Winner gets the river.) Accept?

right.label: Yes. Game on.
right.reaction: The geese won 14-0. They didn't use sticks. They used Gerald.

left.label: No. Shared river.
left.reaction: Gerald has drawn a line down the middle of the river. With his beak. In the ice.

cards.text: Mayor, the ice is starting to creak. I give it until tomorrow morning. Close the rink before then?

right.label: Yes. Close it.
right.reaction: Closed in time. At midnight the ice went 'crack'. Gerald was on it. He's fine. He floated.

left.label: No. One more night.
left.reaction: Everybody skated till dawn. At 6am it cracked. Everyone was home. Except the duck. The duck's fine.

cards.text: Dear Mayor. I built a snowman. He wants to stand for council. His name is Mr Frost. He has a carrot. Can he stand?

right.label: Yes. Mr Frost stands.
right.reaction: Mr Frost is on the ballot. He's polling well. He hasn't said anything. Voters love that.

left.label: No. He's snow.
left.reaction: Timmy is devastated. Mr Frost has been entered as a write-in. In snow. On your car.

cards.text: Mayor, Mr Frost is ahead in the council race. His campaign promise is 'staying cold'. People say it's realistic. Debate him?

right.label: Yes. Debate a snowman.
right.reaction: He said nothing. You said lots. He won. He's very good at saying nothing.

left.label: No. Ignore him.
left.reaction: Ignoring him has made him more popular. He's mysterious now.

cards.text: Dear Mayor. Mr Frost is sad. He's melting a bit. On purpose. It's a protest. Can you say sorry to him?

right.label: Yes. Sorry, Mr Frost.
right.reaction: You apologised to a snowman. On camera. He accepted. His carrot looked moved.

left.label: No. It's weather.
left.reaction: Timmy has told the whole school. You're now known as 'the Snowman Hater'.

cards.text: Mayor. Overnight, forty more snowmen have appeared. All with carrots. All facing City Hall. Same as last week with the cones. Clear them?

right.label: Yes. Clear them.
right.reaction: Cleared. By morning there were eighty. One was wearing your hat.

left.label: No. It's democracy.
left.reaction: The snowmen have formed a party. The Frost Party. Policy: winter.

cards.text: Dear Mayor. The sun is coming out tomorrow. Mr Frost will melt. Can he go in the big freezer at the fish shop?

right.label: Yes. Into the freezer.
right.reaction: Mr Frost is safe. In Sal's freezer. Between the fish. He seems happy. He's re-elected himself.

left.label: No. That's nature.
left.reaction: He melted. Timmy kept the carrot. It's on his windowsill. He talks to it.

cards.text: Boss. We're snowed in at City Hall. Me, you, Doug and the Cheese. The door's blocked. We've got one sandwich. Share it?

right.label: Yes. Share it.
right.reaction: Four bites each. The Cheese didn't eat. Randy ate the Cheese's bite. Morale is high.

left.label: No. Ration it.
left.reaction: Doug has made a spreadsheet for the sandwich. It's very detailed. Nobody's eaten.

cards.text: Boss. We're snowed in. I can dig us out. With a spoon. Might take a month. Let me dig?

right.label: Yes. Dig, Randy.
right.reaction: He dug for six hours. He came out in the basement. Of the library. Linda's furious.

left.label: No. Wait for the plough.
left.reaction: The plough is Bev. She's on her way. At forty miles an hour.

cards.text: Boss. Doug's sandwich spreadsheet has a mistake. Cell B4. I'm owed a crumb. I'd like my crumb. Please?

right.label: Yes. Give him the crumb.
right.reaction: Randy ate the crumb. Slowly. He looked you in the eye the whole time.

left.label: No. Audit it.
left.reaction: You audited the sandwich. It took three hours. The sandwich is gone. Nobody knows how.

cards.text: (Snowed in, the Cheese has started to glow. Faintly. It's warm. Everyone has gathered round it.) Huddle round the Cheese?

right.label: Yes. Huddle.
right.reaction: You all huddled round the Cheese. It hummed. You slept better than you have in years.

left.label: No. Keep away.
left.reaction: You kept away. The cold set in. Doug is wearing the spreadsheet. As a scarf.

cards.text: (Bev has ploughed the door open. With her scooter. She's brought soup.) Thank Bev with a medal?

right.label: Yes. Bev's medal.
right.reaction: Bev's had the medal welded onto the scooter. It's a hood ornament now.

left.label: No. Thanks is enough.
left.reaction: Bev says thanks isn't enough. She's taken the soup back. With interest.

cards.text: Mayor. Bad news. The town's entire supply of road grit is gone. Gerald ate it. All of it. The roads are ice. Buy more?

right.label: Yes. Buy more grit.
right.reaction: Bought. Gerald is guarding it now. Nobody asked him to. He's eaten some.

left.label: No. Use sand.
left.reaction: The beach is now on the roads. Ice-skating has become sand-skating. It's worse.

cards.text: Mayor, I've examined Gerald. He's eaten forty tonnes of grit. He's fine. He's a bit crunchy. He's also very heavy. Can he fly?

right.label: Yes. Let him try.
right.reaction: He took off. Eventually. He's flying very low. He's gritting the roads as he goes.

left.label: No. Rest him.
left.reaction: He's resting in the town square. Children are sledging down him. He's allowing it.

cards.text: Mayor. Your sand ruined my car. It's a sand car now. It's quite nice actually. Want to buy it?

right.label: Yes. Buy the sand car.
right.reaction: It's the official mayoral car. It leaves a trail. You're easy to follow.

left.label: No. Keep your car.
left.reaction: He's entered it in a car show as 'Beach Edition'. It won.

cards.text: (Everyone is sliding to work on the ice. Chief Biscuit would like to give out speeding tickets. To sliders. He's practising his stern face.) Allow it?

right.label: Yes. Ticket them.
right.reaction: Biscuit gave out 400 tickets. Then slid into a lamp post. He's given himself a ticket.

left.label: No. Let them slide.
left.reaction: The town slides everywhere. Work is quicker. Stopping is harder. Bev is loving it.

cards.text: HONK. (Gerald has offered to give the grit back. You would not like how. You can guess how.) Accept his offer?

right.label: Yes. Grit is grit.
right.reaction: The roads are gritted. Nobody wants to talk about how. The geese are very proud.

left.label: No. Keep it.
left.reaction: He's keeping it. He rattles. He's taken up percussion.

cards.text: Mayor, every water pipe in town is frozen. I can thaw them with my heat ray. It might also thaw the Cheese. Use the ray?

right.label: Yes. Fire the ray.
right.reaction: Pipes thawed. The Cheese is also slightly warmer. It's giving off a smell of 1987.

left.label: No. Kettles.
left.reaction: Every kettle in town is pouring into a drain. It's working. Slowly. Doug's counting kettles.

cards.text: Mayor, Nora's heat ray also defrosted Sal's freezer. Mr Frost the snowman is now a puddle. Timmy is in the waiting room. Tell him?

right.label: Yes. Tell him gently.
right.reaction: You told him. He was brave. He asked for the puddle. He's keeping it in a jar.

left.label: No. Build a new one.
left.reaction: Mr Frost II is a bit taller. Timmy says he 'has the same eyes'. It's the same coal.

cards.text: Boss. I've been helping with the kettles. I've boiled 400 kettles. Some of them were the water. Some were soup. The drains smell of soup. Okay?

right.label: Yes. Soup is fine.
right.reaction: The town smells of minestrone. People are sniffing the drains. That's a separate problem.

left.label: No. Water only.
left.reaction: He's switched to water. He's still sad about the soup. He saved a bowl. For you.

cards.text: Mayor, a pipe has burst under the library. The basement is flooded. The 1987 time capsule is floating. Rescue it?

right.label: Yes. Rescue it.
right.reaction: Rescued. Inside: a note from 1987. It says 'DON'T TRUST THE CHEESE'. Interesting.

left.label: No. Books first.
left.reaction: Books saved. The capsule floated out into the river. Gerald is sitting on it.

cards.text: Mayor, the heat ray is still on. It's stuck. It's slowly defrosting the whole town. Spring is coming early. Leave it on?

right.label: Yes. Early spring.
right.reaction: Daffodils in the snow. The geese are confused. Bev has taken her coat off. A first.

left.label: No. Turn it off.
left.reaction: Off. Winter resumed immediately. Everyone sighed. In unison. It was quite loud.

cards.text: Big Carl. Mayor. My pool's frozen. Solid. It's an ice rink now. Am I a lifeguard or an ice guard? I need to know.

right.label: Yes. Ice guard.
right.reaction: He has new skates. And a new whistle. It's frozen. He's blowing it anyway. Silently.

left.label: No. Take a break.
left.reaction: He's taking a break. On the ice. Guarding it. While on a break.

cards.text: Big Carl. Someone fell over on my ice. It was me. I'd like to rescue myself. Officially. Can I file it as a rescue?

right.label: Yes. It counts.
right.reaction: It's his first official rescue. He's framed the form. He's very proud. He's limping.

left.label: No. You fell over.
left.reaction: He's filed it anyway. Under 'near rescue'. It's a new category.

cards.text: Mayor, the Bugle has had a letter. It says Big Carl's ice pool is 'the best thing in Bad Town'. It's from Big Carl. Print it?

right.label: Yes. Print it.
right.reaction: Printed. Seventeen people visited the pool. Carl rescued all of them. None needed it.

left.label: No. Bias.
left.reaction: Carl has written another letter. Signed 'Not Carl'. It's in his handwriting.

cards.text: Mayor! Big Carl's ice pool would be perfect for the Winter Games! Curling! Speed skating! Goose bobsleigh! Book it?

right.label: Yes. Winter Games.
right.reaction: The goose bobsleigh was a highlight. Gerald steered. The sled was Gerald.

left.label: No. Carl's pool.
left.reaction: Carl is relieved. He's had the ice to himself. He's skating in circles. Happily.

cards.text: Big Carl. Mayor. It's thawing tomorrow. Then it'll be a pool. A real pool. Will you come for the first swim?

right.label: Yes. I'll come.
right.reaction: You swam. It was freezing. Carl rescued you. You didn't need it. You'll never tell him.

left.label: No. Too cold.
left.reaction: He swam alone. Then rescued himself. Again. He's going for a record.

cards.text: The PTA is organising the Winter Ball. In City Hall. Tonight. The theme is 'snow'. You'll need a costume. Wear one?

right.label: Yes. Costume.
right.reaction: You came as a snowflake. Gerald came as a snowflake. You were mistaken for each other all night.

left.label: No. Suit.
left.reaction: You came in a suit. Everyone else was snow. You looked like a lamp post. A dog agreed.

cards.text: Boss. I've been asked to DJ the Winter Ball. I have one record. It's of bins. Being emptied. In winter. Can I?

right.label: Yes. DJ Randy.
right.reaction: The bin record was a hit. People danced. Mostly to the lid noises.

left.label: No. Bev's DJing.
left.reaction: DJ Bev is back. She's played the whistling man again. It's become a tradition.

cards.text: Mayor. I'd like to sponsor the Winter Ball. It'll be the ChadBall. There will be a chocolate fountain. And my face in ice. Agree?

right.label: Yes. ChadBall.
right.reaction: The ice sculpture of Chad melted halfway through. Now it's Chad's chin. Just the chin.

left.label: No. Community ball.
left.reaction: Community ball it is. Pam brought sandwiches. 400 of them. All egg.

cards.text: (At midnight, the Cheese arrives at the Winter Ball. On a trolley. Wearing a small bow tie. Nobody invited it.) Let it in?

right.label: Yes. Let it in.
right.reaction: It didn't dance. Everyone danced round it. It was the guest of honour. Somehow.

left.label: No. Cheese out.
left.reaction: The trolley rolled back to the vault. The Cheese's bow tie stayed. It's on the floor. Watching.

cards.text: Boss. Ball's ending. Everyone's asking for a last dance. With you. I've already said yes. On your behalf. Dance?

right.label: Yes. Last dance.
right.reaction: You danced with Randy. Then Bev. Then Gerald. Then Bev again. Best night of the year.

left.label: No. Home time.
left.reaction: You went home. Randy danced alone. To the bin record. Under a disco ball. Which was his.

cards.text: Draft law: ice may only be skated on with written permission. Coach has already submitted forty forms. Sign it?

right.label: Yes. Sign it.
right.reaction: Ninety forms by noon. Doug has approved all of them. He's very cold.

left.label: No. Free skating.
left.reaction: Gerald has skated into City Hall. Through the window. Free skating.

cards.text: Draft law: snowmen may not stand for office. Timmy's at the door with Mr Frost. Sign it?

right.label: Yes. No snowmen.
right.reaction: Mr Frost has been disqualified. He's standing outside your window. Silently. As always.

left.label: No. Snow rights.
left.reaction: Mr Frost is officially a candidate. His running mate is a carrot.

cards.text: Draft law: the Cheese must be kept at a safe distance from all mayors. Doug wrote it. He's hiding behind the door. Sign it?

right.label: Yes. Safe distance.
right.reaction: The Cheese is now three metres from you at all times. It feels further. It feels closer.

left.label: No. It's fine.
left.reaction: The Cheese has been moved into your office. Nobody admits doing it.

cards.text: Draft law: geese may not eat road grit. Gerald has eaten the draft. Sign the photocopy?

right.label: Yes. Sign it.
right.reaction: Signed. Gerald has eaten the photocopy. And the photocopier. He rattles.

left.label: No. He's suffered enough.
left.reaction: Gerald has been pardoned. He's eaten the pardon. He's never been happier.

cards.text: Draft law: heat rays must be licensed. Nora's has been on since Tuesday. Sign it?

right.label: Yes. License them.
right.reaction: Nora has a licence. It's laminated. She melted the lamination with the ray.

left.label: No. Science is free.
left.reaction: Three new heat rays by teatime. One is a hairdryer. Brayden.

cards.text: Draft law: every pool must have a lifeguard. Bad Town has one pool. It's ice. Big Carl is weeping with joy. Sign it?

right.label: Yes. Carl's law.
right.reaction: Carl is now required by law. He's printed it on his towel. And his whistle.

left.label: No. Carl volunteers.
left.reaction: Carl volunteers anyway. Harder. He's been there since 4am.

cards.text: Draft law: every Winter Ball must have a last dance. Pam wrote it. She's holding the pen out. Sign it?

right.label: Yes. Last dances.
right.reaction: Signed. Tonight's last dance lasted until 3am. Nobody could agree which was last.

left.label: No. Optional dancing.
left.reaction: Pam is disappointed. She's dancing anyway. Defiantly.

cards.text: Stormy Steve. I forecast sunshine. So, naturally, it's a blizzard. The worst in forty years. Everyone's stuck. Send the snowplough?

right.label: Yes. Send it.
right.reaction: The snowplough is Bev. She's cleared every street. And one or two gardens.

left.label: No. Snow day.
left.reaction: Snow day. Nobody went to work. Shops shut. Everyone built snowmen. One is running for council.

cards.text: Mayor. Bev ploughed my garden. My statues are buried. All forty-one. Each one is me. Dig them out?

right.label: Yes. Dig them out.
right.reaction: Forty-one Chads, freshly dug. He's thrilled. The town's quieter without them.

left.label: No. Spring will.
left.reaction: Children are building snowmen on top of them. Chad is ninety percent snowman now.

cards.text: Mayor, a snow day costs the town a fortune. Nobody's buying anything. I've worked it out. It's... a lot. One more?

right.label: Yes. One more.
right.reaction: Two snow days. The happiest town in the county. The poorest, too. Doug's ok.

left.label: No. Back to work.
left.reaction: Everyone's back. Grumpy. Snow in their shoes. Productivity is up. Morale is not.

cards.text: EMERGENCY. Someone's built a sledge run from the top of the clock tower. It ends in the town square. Children are queuing. Close it?

right.label: Yes. Close it.
right.reaction: Closed. The children have built a new sledge run. Down the library steps. Linda is furious.

left.label: No. Let them sledge.
left.reaction: Best day ever. One sledge overshot. Into the fountain. It was Randy. He's fine.

cards.text: Mayor. There are children sledging down the library steps. They're shushing each other as they go. It's very polite. Allow it?

right.label: Yes. Quiet sledging.
right.reaction: Silent sledging. Very respectful. Linda has issued library cards to the sledges.

left.label: No. Not the library.
left.reaction: Sledging has moved to the town hall steps. Right outside your window.

cards.text: Boss. I built the sledge run. It's a business. I'm charging. In crisps. Business is very good. Can I keep it?

right.label: Yes. Randy's run.
right.reaction: It's the most profitable thing in Bad Town. He's paid tax. In crisps. Doug's eating them.

left.label: No. Shut it down.
left.reaction: Shut down. Randy is sulking. He's using it himself. Over and over.

cards.text: Mayor. The town hall heating has broken. It's minus four in here. Randy's put on four coats. They're all the same coat. Fix it?

right.label: Yes. Fix it.
right.reaction: The heating's fixed. It's now forty degrees. Everyone's in shorts. Doug is wearing a spreadsheet.

left.label: No. Wear jumpers.
left.reaction: Everyone's in jumpers. Doug knitted one for the Cheese. The Cheese seems warmer.

cards.text: Mayor, the heating's stuck at forty degrees. The Cheese is sweating. It's forming a puddle. The puddle is moving. Turn it down?

right.label: Yes. Turn it down.
right.reaction: Turned down. The puddle has stopped. Pointing at you. Coincidence.

left.label: No. Leave it.
left.reaction: The puddle has reached the door. It's leaving the building. Where's it going?

cards.text: Boss. I've been wearing four coats. I can't take them off. The cousins are frozen to the lining. Help?

right.label: Yes. Help him.
right.reaction: Unfrozen. Forty cousins came out. One by one. Each thanked you personally.

left.label: No. Stay warm.
left.reaction: He's staying in the coats. All winter. He waddles. Like Mr Flaps.

cards.text: BREAKING. A small avalanche on Bad Hill. Nobody hurt. But it buried Sal's restaurant. The diners are still eating. Dig them out?

right.label: Yes. Dig them out.
right.reaction: Dug out. The diners asked for the bill. Sal charged them for the snow.

left.label: No. They're eating.
left.reaction: They finished pudding. Then dug themselves out. Five stars. Atmospheric.

cards.text: Mayor. The avalanche has given me an idea. Igloo dining. You eat in snow. Under snow. It's the future. Approve the licence?

right.label: Yes. Igloo dining.
right.reaction: Fully booked till spring. The tyres stay frozen. People say they're crunchier.

left.label: No. It's dangerous.
left.reaction: He's opened anyway. In a fridge. A big fridge. Same thing, he says.

cards.text: (Lorraine the seagull has been seen at the top of Bad Hill. With a very large chip. She drops it. Another avalanche.) Arrest her?

right.label: Yes. Arrest her.
right.reaction: Arrested. She escaped through the window. With the arrest warrant. And Barb's chips.

left.label: No. It's a chip.
left.reaction: Three more avalanches. Each with a chip. Lorraine's very pleased. She's started a business.

cards.text: EMERGENCY. An iceberg has floated up the river. A real one. It's stuck under the bridge. It has a penguin on it. Keep it?

right.label: Yes. Keep the iceberg.
right.reaction: The iceberg is a tourist attraction. The penguin is called Dennis. Everyone loves Dennis.

left.label: No. Push it out.
left.reaction: Pushed. It floated back. Dennis waved.

cards.text: HONK. (Gerald and Dennis the penguin are having a stand-off. On the iceberg. Neither has blinked in four hours.) Intervene?

right.label: Yes. Separate them.
right.reaction: Separated. Gerald is furious. Dennis is very calm. Dennis has won.

left.label: No. Let them settle it.
left.reaction: They're best friends now. Dennis has joined the Goose Union. The first non-goose. He's treasurer.

cards.text: Mayor. The iceberg keeps floating back. With the penguin. He's started waving. People are waving back. Do something?

right.label: Yes. Rehome Dennis.
right.reaction: Dennis has a pond. With the geese. He's learning to honk. It sounds like a cough.

left.label: No. Wave back.
left.reaction: Everyone waves at Dennis. Every morning. He waves back. He's the most popular person in Bad Town.

cards.text: Big Carl. Mayor. EMERGENCY. Someone's on thin ice. It's Gerald. He's sitting there. On purpose. Can I go in?

right.label: Yes. Go in.
right.reaction: Carl dived in. Gerald stood up. Walked off. Carl is in the river. Rescuing himself. Again.

left.label: No. Gerald floats.
left.reaction: Gerald fell through. He floated. He honked. He's fine. Carl is crying with frustration.

cards.text: Big Carl. I rescued myself again. That's my fourth this week. Is there a medal? There should be a medal.

right.label: Yes. A medal.
right.reaction: Medal of Self-Rescue. He's the only holder. He's the only possible holder.

left.label: No. Stop falling in.
left.reaction: He's taken that advice. He's wearing a life jacket. Indoors.

cards.text: HONK. (Gerald would like to complain about being rescued. He wasn't rescued. He'd still like to complain.) Hear him out?

right.label: Yes. Hear him out.
right.reaction: He honked for nine minutes. You nodded. He felt heard. He left a feather.

left.label: No. Nobody rescued you.
left.reaction: He's filing a formal complaint. Against the river.

cards.text: EMERGENCY. Everything's thawing at once. All of it. The town is one big puddle. Ankle-deep. Rising. Sandbags?

right.label: Yes. Sandbags.
right.reaction: Sandbagged. The water's gone round. Into the next town. They've sent a strongly worded letter.

left.label: No. Wellies for all.
left.reaction: Wellies for everyone. The town is wading. Bev has a boat.

cards.text: Mayor, the next town says our thaw has flooded them. They want an apology. And a mop. Send both?

right.label: Yes. Both.
right.reaction: Apology sent. Mop sent. They've sent the mop back. Wetter.

left.label: No. Weather is weather.
left.reaction: The next town has declared a cold war. It's appropriate. It's winter.

cards.text: Big Carl. Mayor. The whole town is ankle-deep water. Technically, it's all a pool now. I'm on duty. Everywhere. Okay?

right.label: Yes. Guard everything.
right.reaction: Carl has never been happier. He's guarded the whole town. Rescued four ducks. They didn't need it.

left.label: No. Rest, Carl.
left.reaction: He's resting. Standing in the water. With his whistle. Just in case.

cards.text: Mayor, the 1987 cheese in the vault has moved. Six inches. Towards the door. Lock the vault?

right.label: Yes. Lock it.
right.reaction: Locked. You heard a small sound behind the door. Like cheese settling. Or waiting.

left.label: No. Let it roam.
left.reaction: Doug left the door ajar. By morning the cheese was in the corridor. Facing your office.

cards.text: Mayor, I've studied the cheese. It hasn't moved. The vault has. Slowly. Towards the cheese. Should I worry?

right.label: Yes. Worry.
right.reaction: Nora is worrying professionally. She's bought a clipboard. It's shaking.

left.label: No. It's cheese.
left.reaction: 'It's cheese,' you said. The vault creaked. Doug has started sleeping at home.

cards.text: Boss. The cheese is outside your office. I said hello. It didn't say hello back. But I felt it. Let it in?

right.label: Yes. Let it in.
right.reaction: It's in your office. On a trolley. Facing your desk. It feels like a meeting.

left.label: No. Back to the vault.
left.reaction: Randy wheeled it back. He came out pale. He won't say what it said.

cards.text: Mayor, the 1987 council minutes mention the cheese. Once. They say: 'DO NOT LET IT NEAR THE CHAIR.' Which chair, do you think?

right.label: Yes. Find out.
right.reaction: The minutes continue on page 2. Page 2 is missing. There's a cheese stain where it was.

left.label: No. Don't want to know.
left.reaction: Linda has filed the minutes under 'Ominous'. It's a new section.

cards.text: (This morning the cheese is on your chair. Your mayor's chair. Beside it, a small card: 'ACTING'.) Remove it?

right.label: Yes. Remove it.
right.reaction: Removed. The chair is warm. Faintly cheese-scented. You sit on it anyway. Bravely.

left.label: No. Let it act.
left.reaction: It's acting mayor for the day. You worked from the beanbag. Nobody noticed.

cards.text: Mayor, the cheese is back in the vault behind three locks. It seems patient. A fourth lock?

right.label: Yes. Four locks.
right.reaction: Four locks. Doug checks them hourly. Last night all four were warm.

left.label: No. Three is plenty.
left.reaction: Three locks. The cheese seems to accept this. For now.

cards.text: Mayor, the cheese has been acting mayor for a day. Approval is up 9%. It hasn't done anything. People find that restful. Let it carry on?

right.label: Yes. Let it rest.
right.reaction: It carried on. It signed nothing. Crime fell. Nobody can explain it.

left.label: No. My job.
left.reaction: You took your chair back. The cheese was wheeled out to light applause.

cards.text: Boss. The cheese is locked up. But every morning there's a small cheese-shaped dent in your chair. Investigate?

right.label: Yes. Investigate.
right.reaction: You stayed up all night. Nothing came. At dawn there was a dent. You'd blinked.

left.label: No. It's a nice dent.
left.reaction: You sit in the dent now. It fits you perfectly. That's the worrying part.

cards.text: (The cheese holds a press conference. It says nothing. The town hangs on every silence. There's one seat left on stage. Behind it.) Take the seat?

right.label: Yes. Sit behind it.
right.reaction: You sat behind the cheese. You've been behind it ever since.

left.label: No. Stand beside it.
left.reaction: You stood beside it. Equals. The cheese seemed to respect that.

cards.text: Mayor, test results: 1987 cheddar. Normal. Except it's warm, and it hums when you say its name. Leave it alone?

right.label: Yes. Leave it alone.
right.reaction: You've left it alone. It hums softly. It sounds almost like a lullaby.

left.label: No. One more test.
left.reaction: Nora said its name into a microphone. The lights dimmed. She's stopped testing.

cards.text: (The cheese has proposed a fondue. For the whole town. At the Winter Ball. You're guest of honour. In the middle. Of the fondue.) Agree?

right.label: Yes. Fondue it is.
right.reaction: Doug has ordered a cauldron. A big one. Bigger than you. He measured.

left.label: No fondue.
left.reaction: No fondue. The cheese went very quiet. Quieter than usual.

cards.text: (Last night of the week. The cheese has sent you a card. It's blank. It smells of cheese. It feels like a thank you.) Keep the card?

right.label: Yes. Keep it.
right.reaction: It's on your desk. Still warm. You feel strangely safe.

left.label: No. Bin it.
left.reaction: Randy rescued it from the bin. It's in the coat now. For luck.

cards.text: (The Winter Ball. A cauldron of fondue bubbles. The cheese sits beside it on its trolley. There's a little step. For you.) Step in?

right.label: Yes. Step in.
right.reaction: It was warm. Very warm. Then it was everything.

left.label: No. Dip some bread.
left.reaction: You dipped one piece of bread. The cheese seemed satisfied. For now.

cards.text: Coach Dunk is about to skate onto thin ice. Swap his skates for wellies while he's not looking.

right.label: Swapped them
right.reaction: He's in wellies. On the bank. Skating motions. He hasn't noticed.

left.label: Caught
left.reaction: He caught you holding his skate. 'You want to join the team?' You're on the team now.

cards.text: Mr Frost's campaign office opens today. Gerald is waddling at the ribbon, face first. Cut it before he does!

right.label: Snip!
right.reaction: Open. Mr Frost said nothing. Timmy said it was his best speech.

left.label: Gerald got there
left.reaction: Gerald cut it, then ate Mr Frost's carrot. Timmy is inconsolable.

cards.text: Randy is eating the last sandwich. Again. Grab it back while he's not looking.

right.label: Got it
right.reaction: You've got the sandwich. Half of it. Randy has the other half. In the coat.

left.label: Caught
left.reaction: He turned round, sandwich in mouth. He offered you the crust. It was a kind gesture.

cards.text: The new grit store opens today. Gerald is racing at the ribbon. He's hungry. Cut it first!

right.label: Snip!
right.reaction: Open. Full of grit. Barb's guarding it. Gerald's guarding Barb.

left.label: Gerald got there
left.reaction: Gerald cut it. Then went in. Then came out. Then the grit was gone.

cards.text: Nora is about to turn the heat ray up to eleven. Unplug it while she's not looking.

right.label: Unplugged
right.reaction: Unplugged. The ray powered down. Nora thinks it was a power cut. She's suing the power.

left.label: Caught
left.reaction: She caught you holding the plug. She's given you a lab coat. You're her assistant now.

cards.text: Big Carl's ice pool reopens today. Gerald is skating at the ribbon. Fast. Cut it first!

right.label: Snip!
right.reaction: Open. Carl blew his frozen whistle. A tiny icicle came out. He's thrilled.

left.label: Gerald got there
left.reaction: Gerald cut it with his face. At speed. He's still sliding. He's past the town now.

cards.text: Chad is changing the Winter Ball sign to 'CHADBALL'. Swap it back while he's not looking.

right.label: Swapped it
right.reaction: It's the Winter Ball again. Chad doesn't know. He's introducing himself as host.

left.label: Caught
left.reaction: He caught you mid-swap. Now it says 'CHADBALL (WINTER)'. A compromise.

cards.text: Mr Flaps. The snow has closed the roads. I'll deliver by beak. It's a long way. I'll need more fish. Approve the fish budget?

right.label: Yes. More fish.
right.reaction: Every letter delivered. Slightly fishy. Bev got her pension. In a herring.

left.label: No. Post can wait.
left.reaction: The post is waiting. In Mr Flaps. He's very round. He's practically a snowman.

cards.text: The PTA's winter fair invitations went out by pelican. They arrived damp. They now say 'WINTER F'. Reprint them?

right.label: Yes. Reprint.
right.reaction: Reprinted. Sent by Mr Flaps. Arrived damp. Now say 'NTER FAI'. Progress.

left.label: No. Winter F it is.
left.reaction: 'Winter F' was a huge success. Nobody knew what it was. Everybody came.

cards.text: (Pebbles is eating the snowmen. Only the carrots. Every snowman in town looks very surprised.) Stop him?

right.label: Yes. Stop him.
right.reaction: Stopped. He's eaten the 'Stop' sign on his way past.

left.label: No. He needs vitamins.
left.reaction: Forty carrots eaten. Forty surprised snowmen. Mr Frost is next. Timmy is guarding him.

cards.text: Dear Mayor. The goat is looking at Mr Frost's carrot. I have a stick. It's for pointing. Can you help?

right.label: Yes. Guard Mr Frost.
right.reaction: You stood guard. Pebbles ate your scarf instead. Mr Frost is safe. Timmy is thrilled.

left.label: No. Let nature decide.
left.reaction: Pebbles ate the carrot. Mr Frost now has a parsnip. Timmy says he looks 'different'.

cards.text: Wooo. Mayor. It's very cold. Ghosts feel the cold. I'd like a hot water bottle. It'll fall through me. I'd still like one.

right.label: Yes. Hot water bottle.
right.reaction: It fell through her. Into the basement. Wendy says it's the thought that counts.

left.label: No. You're a ghost.
left.reaction: She's haunting the boiler room. For warmth. The pipes are making woo noises.

cards.text: Wooo. I've found a way to keep warm. I'm haunting Doug's cardigan. He hasn't noticed. Can I stay?

right.label: Yes. Stay warm.
right.reaction: Doug's cardigan says 'wooo' when he sits down. He thinks it's his back. It's not.

left.label: No. Leave Doug alone.
left.reaction: She's haunting your scarf now. It's very warm. It sighs.

cards.text: (Trevor the moth has found the warmest lamp in Bad Town. It's your desk lamp. He's moved in. He's very happy.) Let him stay?

right.label: Yes. Stay, Trevor.
right.reaction: He lives on your lamp. He watches you work. He's very supportive.

left.label: No. Shoo.
left.reaction: He's moved to the lamp in the corridor. He looks at you every time you pass.

cards.text: (Trevor has brought friends. Forty moths. All on your lamp. It's dim now. They're very happy.) Get a second lamp?

right.label: Yes. Second lamp.
right.reaction: Two lamps. Eighty moths. One very bright office. You need sunglasses indoors.

left.label: No. Work in the dark.
left.reaction: You're working by moth. It flickers. You've signed four things you didn't mean to.

cards.text: (Professor Hoot wants to cancel school for snow. It isn't snowing at the school. He'd just like a nap.) Cancel school?

right.label: Yes. Snow day.
right.reaction: No school. The children built Hoot a snow nest. He's asleep in it. Peacefully.

left.label: No school's open.
left.reaction: School's open. Hoot is asleep at his desk. The children are teaching the lesson. On owls.

cards.text: The PTA has noticed Professor Hoot sleeps all day. They'd like a daytime deputy head. Approve one?

right.label: Yes. A day deputy.
right.reaction: The new deputy is Bev. She's been a deputy head before. In 1952. She's very strict.

left.label: No. Owls are owls.
left.reaction: The school is run at night now. Officially. The children are nocturnal. Parents are tired.

cards.text: (Toby the oak tree is cold. He'd like a scarf. A big one. Forty metres.) Knit Toby a scarf?

right.label: Yes. Knit it.
right.reaction: The whole town knitted. Forty metres of scarf. Toby has never looked so cosy.

left.label: No. Trees are fine.
left.reaction: He's dropped every icicle on the town hall steps. One at a time. Pointedly.

cards.text: (Toby would like matching mittens. For his branches. There are two hundred branches.) Knit mittens?

right.label: Yes. Two hundred mittens.
right.reaction: Two hundred mittens. Every squirrel in town lives in one now. Mr Nutkins charges rent.

left.label: No. One scarf is plenty.
left.reaction: He's sulking. Slowly. Over several weeks. Trees sulk long.

cards.text: (Kevin the pothole has frozen over. Children are skating in him. He seems delighted.) Put up a sign?

right.label: Yes. 'Kevin's Rink'.
right.reaction: Kevin's Rink is the most popular attraction in town. He's very deep. And very still.

left.label: No. Grit him.
left.reaction: Gritted. The children are sad. Kevin is crunchy now.

cards.text: (Clive the traffic cone is wearing a snow hat. Nobody put it there. He looks very pleased with himself.) Take it off?

right.label: Yes. Take it off.
right.reaction: Removed. By morning, a new hat. Knitted. In his colours. Someone's on his side.

left.label: No. It suits him.
left.reaction: He's been voted 'Best Dressed Cone'. He's the only entrant. He won anyway.

cards.text: (Gary the vending machine has frozen. Every can is a slushie now. He's selling them as 'winter specials'.) Allow it?

right.label: Yes. Winter specials.
right.reaction: Sold out. Everyone's brain is frozen. Gary is very pleased. He's humming in C.

left.label: No. Thaw him.
left.reaction: Thawed. Everything fizzed out at once. Gary's display reads 'SORRY'. Again.

cards.text: (Reginald the tortoise has gone into hibernation. In the middle of the road. Again.) Move him?

right.label: Yes. Gently.
right.reaction: Moved to the pavement. He woke up for one second. He went back to the road.

left.label: No. Divert traffic.
left.reaction: Traffic goes round him. Very slowly. Out of respect. And caution.

cards.text: (Reginald is back in the road. Sleeping. Chief Biscuit would like to give him a parking ticket. He's already written it.) Allow it?

right.label: Yes. Ticket him.
right.reaction: Ticketed. He'll read it in April. He'll pay it in 2031.

left.label: No. He's sleeping.
left.reaction: Biscuit has curled up next to him. Two sleeping officers of the road.

cards.text: Mr Nutkins. Squirrel Bank. I've buried the bank's reserves for winter. I can't remember where. I need a short-term loan. From you. Approve?

right.label: Yes. Lend him some.
right.reaction: Lent. By spring he'll find the reserves. Under your car. Under all of it.

left.label: No. Dig harder.
left.reaction: He's digging up the park. Every hole has an acorn. None of them are his.

cards.text: Mr Nutkins. I've found the reserves. They're under the town hall. Directly under. May I dig?

right.label: Yes. Dig.
right.reaction: He dug. The town hall now leans. Slightly. Nobody's mentioned it.

left.label: No. Wait for spring.
left.reaction: He's waiting. On your doorstep. Every morning. Looking at the floor.

cards.text: (Inspector Biscuit would like a winter coat. With a badge. And four sleeves.) Approve the uniform budget?

right.label: Yes. Four sleeves.
right.reaction: He looks magnificent. He's arrested three snowmen just to show it off.

left.label: No. You have fur.
left.reaction: He's filed a grievance. With his paw. On your trousers.

cards.text: (Marcel the mime is miming being cold. Very convincingly. People are giving him blankets. Real ones.) Intervene?

right.label: Yes. He's fine.
right.reaction: You told everyone he's fine. He mimed being hurt by that. Very convincingly.

left.label: No. More blankets.
left.reaction: He has forty blankets. He's mimed a fireplace. People are sitting round it.

cards.text: Mr Whiskers Esq. is suing the snow. It sat on his chair. Without permission. He'd like the town to pay damages.

right.label: Yes. Pay the cat.
right.reaction: Paid. He's spent it on a heated chair. He's suing the next snowfall in advance.

left.label: No. Snow can't be sued.
left.reaction: He's taking it to a higher court. It's Barb's helicopter.

cards.text: (Lorraine the seagull has stolen every scarf from the lost property. She's wearing all of them. She can't fly.) Get them back?

right.label: Yes. Get them back.
right.reaction: Unwound. Took an hour. She went round and round. She's dizzy. Not sorry.

left.label: No. She's cold too.
left.reaction: She's waddling round town in forty scarves. People are calling her 'the Duchess'. She loves it.

cards.text: (Lorraine is back. She's brought you a scarf. It's yours. She stole it this morning. It's a gift now.) Accept?

right.label: Yes. Thank you.
right.reaction: You thanked a seagull for your own scarf. She seemed genuinely moved.

left.label: No. It's mine.
left.reaction: She's kept it. She wears it on your windowsill. Every morning.

cards.text: Mayor, I'd like to go wild swimming in the frozen lake. Through a hole. I've already cut the hole. Coming?

right.label: Yes. I'll come.
right.reaction: You lasted four seconds. Bev did forty minutes. She says you're 'soft'.

left.label: No. Big Carl can.
left.reaction: Carl went in to supervise. Bev had to rescue him. Again.

cards.text: Big Carl. Bev has rescued me eleven times this year. I'd like to give her my whistle. As a thank you. Is that allowed?

right.label: Yes. Give it to her.
right.reaction: She's wearing it. She blew it at a bus. The bus stopped. She's keeping it.

left.label: No. You need it.
left.reaction: He's kept it. He's bought her a second whistle. She's blowing both.

cards.text: Dear Mayor. It isn't snowing at school. Only at my house. I'm very sure. Can I have a snow day?

right.label: Yes. Timmy's snow day.
right.reaction: Snow day for one. He built a snowman. It's running for council.

left.label: No. To school.
left.reaction: He went. He told everyone it snowed at his house. Everyone believed him.

cards.text: Mayor, the library's 'How to Survive Winter' was borrowed in 1987. It's never come back. Shall we send a search party?

right.label: Yes. Find that book.
right.reaction: Found. In the cheese vault. It's warm. The cheese seems to have been reading it.

left.label: No. Buy another.
left.reaction: New copy bought. It has a 400-year waiting list. Mostly Bev.

cards.text: Mayor, the book we found in the cheese vault has notes in the margins. In very small letters. They say 'SOON'. Return it to the shelf?

right.label: Yes. Shelve it.
right.reaction: Shelved. Under 'Not Ominous'. Linda has moved the shelf further away.

left.label: No. Burn the notes.
left.reaction: You can't burn them. They're cheese. They melted. Now the whole book says SOON.

cards.text: Mayor. I'm selling hot soup. In tyres. The tyres keep it warm. Will you try one?

right.label: Yes. Try one.
right.reaction: It's soup. Warm, tyre-y soup. Four thousand sold. The tyres are refillable.

left.label: No thank you.
left.reaction: Gerald tried it. He liked it. He tried the tyre. He liked that too.

cards.text: Mayor, the Bugle's Best Snowman competition. Mr Frost has entered. Timmy is his campaign manager. Is it rigged?

right.label: Yes. Investigate.
right.reaction: It's rigged. In favour of Mr Frost. Timmy did it. With a crayon. He's eight.

left.label: No. Let it run.
left.reaction: Mr Frost won. He said nothing. Timmy cried. The carrot looked proud.

cards.text: Dear Mayor. Yes I rigged it. Mr Frost deserved it. He is very good at standing. Am I in trouble?

right.label: Yes. A little.
right.reaction: He's been banned from rigging for a week. He's rigging something else. You can feel it.

left.label: No. Good job.
left.reaction: Timmy's been hired by Chad. As a consultant. He's earning more than Doug.

cards.text: Mayor! Heated socks! App-controlled! They only work on Wi-Fi! So, indoors. Stay indoors! Approve them?

right.label: Yes. Heated socks.
right.reaction: Everyone's feet are warm. Nobody's leaving the house. Business is booming. Indoors.

left.label: No. Normal socks.
left.reaction: Brayden has sold four thousand anyway. Everyone's standing near the router.

cards.text: Mayor! Ice fishing! I've never caught a fish! This is the year! Can I use the town hall pond? It's frozen!

right.label: Yes. Fish, Coach.
right.reaction: Six hours. No fish. He caught a boot. He's coached it. It's doing well.

left.label: No. There are no fish.
left.reaction: There are fish. Three. They're watching him. Smugly. Through the ice.

cards.text: Mayor! I caught a fish! It's Gerald! He bit the line! Do I keep him?

right.label: Yes. Catch and keep.
right.reaction: Gerald has been weighed. He's a record. He's honking about it. Coach is crying.

left.label: No. Catch and release.
left.reaction: Released. Gerald immediately bit the line again. They're doing it all day.

cards.text: Mayor. I'd like to turn the heating down one degree. It saves £3. Per year. Everyone will be furious. Do it?

right.label: Yes. One degree.
right.reaction: Down one degree. The office is wearing hats. Randy is wearing two coats. Again.

left.label: No. Stay warm.
left.reaction: Doug is turning it down in secret. Half a degree. At night. Everyone suspects.

cards.text: Stormy Steve. I forecast snow. Which means sun. I've been wrong six weeks running. Am I due a right one?

right.label: Yes. You're due.
right.reaction: It snowed. He was right. He's in shock. He's handed in his resignation. Doug refused it.

left.label: No. Stay wrong.
left.reaction: It was sunny. He was wrong. Everyone was relieved. It's tradition now.

cards.text: The PTA wants a winter fair. In the car park. On the ice. Stalls, games and a coconut shy. With snowballs. Approve it?

right.label: Yes. Winter fair.
right.reaction: Best fair in years. Bev won the coconut shy. Then the coconuts. Then the shy.

left.label: No. Too icy.
left.reaction: They held it in the library. Linda shushed every stall.

cards.text: The winter fair made £400! The PTA would like to spend it on a hot chocolate fountain. For the school. Allow it?

right.label: Yes. Hot chocolate.
right.reaction: The fountain is a triumph. The school smells of chocolate. Exam results are up. Somehow.

left.label: No. Books.
left.reaction: 400 books. All about hot chocolate. The children are reading. Angrily.

cards.text: Boss. I built a snow-raccoon. It's bigger than me. It's wearing my coat. I'm cold. Can I have the coat back?

right.label: Yes. Take it back.
right.reaction: He took the coat. The snow-raccoon looks sad. He gave it a scarf. Out of guilt.

left.label: No. It's art.
left.reaction: It's in the Bugle: 'GIANT SNOW RACCOON'. Randy is shivering in the photo. Proudly.

cards.text: Mayor. I'd like to heat the whole high street. With a giant patio heater. Shaped like me. It's ninety feet. Allow it?

right.label: Yes. Heat the street.
right.reaction: It's lovely and warm. Snow has melted in a Chad-shaped circle. Visible from space.

left.label: No. It's ninety feet.
left.reaction: He's built it on his own lawn. Facing the high street. Pointedly.

cards.text: Mayor, the giant Chad heater is melting the clock tower. It's leaning. Towards the heater. Turn it off?

right.label: Yes. Off.
right.reaction: Off. The clock tower straightened. Mostly. It's two minutes slow now.

left.label: No. Lean with it.
left.reaction: The clock tower has leaned all the way. It's resting on Chad. He's fine. He's charging rent.

cards.text: HONK. (Gerald would like to migrate. He has never migrated. He'd like a leaving party. He has packed a bag. It's bread.) Throw the party?

right.label: Yes. Farewell, Gerald.
right.reaction: The party was lovely. He left. He came back an hour later. He'd forgotten his bread.

left.label: No. Stay.
left.reaction: He stayed. He's very relieved. He's unpacked the bread. And eaten it.

cards.text: HONK. (Gerald would like a second leaving party. He promises to actually leave this time.) Throw another?

right.label: Yes. One more.
right.reaction: Second party. He left. He came back in the morning. He'd migrated to the next street.

left.label: No. You live here.
left.reaction: He agreed. He's unpacked. He's never been happier. He honked about it all night.

cards.text: Mayor, I've made artificial snow. It's warm. It's pink. It's everywhere. It smells of strawberries. Keep it?

right.label: Yes. Pink snow.
right.reaction: The town is pink. Children are eating it. Nora says it's 'probably' fine.

left.label: No. Normal snow.
left.reaction: Hosed away. The river runs pink. The ducks are thrilled. They smell of strawberries.

cards.text: Big Carl. I'm on duty at the frozen fountain. Someone dropped a coin. I'm chipping it out. It's been six hours. Keep going?

right.label: Yes. Keep going.
right.reaction: Nine hours. He got it. It was 2p. He gave it to Doug. Doug cried. Again.

left.label: No. Let it go.
left.reaction: He let it go. He comes back every day. Just to look at it.

cards.text: Mr Flaps. I have delivered a parcel. It's a snowball. From the next town. Addressed to you. Return to sender?

right.label: Yes. Send it back.
right.reaction: Sent back. By beak. It arrived as water. They've sent a strongly worded puddle.

left.label: No. Throw it back.
left.reaction: You threw it. It hit the next town's mayor. On television. Snowball war declared.

cards.text: Mayor, the next town has declared a snowball war. They're massing on the border. With snow. Fight back?

right.label: Yes. Snowball war!
right.reaction: Bad Town won. Mostly thanks to Bev. And her scooter. And the geese.

left.label: No. Make peace.
left.reaction: Peace treaty signed. In snow. It melted at lunch. War resumed.

cards.text: (Councillor Pebbles is sitting in your seat at the council meeting. He's chewing something. It's the agenda. Again.) Start without it?

right.label: Yes. Wing it.
right.reaction: You winged it. It was the best meeting in years. Pebbles abstained. With his mouth full.

left.label: No. Reprint the agenda.
left.reaction: Reprinted. He ate that too. The printer has fled.

cards.text: Crime is up. Someone's stealing snowmen's carrots. Every carrot in town. It's organised. Hire more officers?

right.label: Yes. More officers.
right.reaction: Four new officers. All snowmen. They're very good at standing guard.

left.label: No. Do your best.
left.reaction: Barb's on carrot watch. Alone. With a flask. She's seen things.

cards.text: There's a protest outside City Hall. About the cold. They've brought placards and a brazier. They've lit the placards. Talk to them?

right.label: Yes. Talk to them.
right.reaction: You listened. You brought soup. They've forgiven you. For now.

left.label: No. Wait it out.
left.reaction: They've built an igloo. It's got a kettle. They're never leaving.

cards.text: Mayor. The freeze has cost everything. I've sold my winter coat. I'm in a duvet. Sell the town's snowplough?

right.label: Yes. Sell the plough.
right.reaction: Sold. Bev is the snowplough now. Officially. She's charging.

left.label: No. Tax the snow.
left.reaction: Snow tax. Per flake. Doug is counting. He'll be some time.

cards.text: Mayor. Business is frozen. Literally. My shops are shut. Everyone's shut. Give a winter grant?

right.label: Yes. Winter grant.
right.reaction: Shops are open. Doors are warm. Chad has used his grant on a hot tub. For 'business'.

left.label: No. Wait for spring.
left.reaction: Everyone's waiting for spring. In the shops. With the lights off.

cards.text: Business is booming! Even in the freeze! I'd like to buy the snow. All of it. Then sell it back. Agree?

right.label: Yes. Sell the snow.
right.reaction: Chad owns the snow. It's £2 a snowball. Children are furious.

left.label: No.
left.reaction: He's bought the clouds instead. It's unclear how. Doug's checking.

cards.text: Mayor! The ice has a sign: 'THIN ICE. ESPECIALLY MAYORS.' That's probably about the old mayor. Skate out to the middle with me?

right.label: Yes. Let's skate.
right.reaction: It was about you.

left.label: No. I'll watch.
left.reaction: Coach went alone. He went through. Carl saved him. Again.

cards.text: Dear Mayor. Mr Frost wants to swap places tonight: he sits in your office, you stand outside. It's minus twenty tonight. Swap?

right.label: Yes. Swap.
right.reaction: You stood out in the snow all night. Very still. Like a professional.

left.label: No. Sorry, Mr Frost.
left.reaction: Mr Frost said nothing. Timmy said a lot. Then forgave you. For a biscuit.

cards.text: Boss. Still snowed in. Wait for Bev's plough? Or take the shortcut through the cheese vault. Doug says nobody who goes in comes out.

right.label: Yes. Wait for Bev.
right.reaction: Bev ploughed the door open. The vault stayed shut. Something in there sighed.

left.label: No. Take the shortcut.
left.reaction: The cheese let you in. It did not let you out.

cards.text: HONK. (Gerald offers you his grit. All of it. He'll bring it up for you, right now, on live television. You know how.) Accept on camera?

right.label: Yes. Live on air.
right.reaction: You accepted. On live television.

left.label: No, thank you.
left.reaction: He's very relieved. So is everyone. So is the camera.

cards.text: Mayor, the heat ray is stuck on full. Shall I just pull the plug? Or someone could press the off switch. It's on the front. Where the ray comes out.

right.label: Yes. Pull the plug.
right.reaction: Pulled. The ray died. Spring paused. Nora sulked.

left.label: No. I'll press the switch.
left.reaction: You pressed the switch. The ray pressed back.

cards.text: Big Carl. The ice pool's thawing. The sign says DANGER: VERY DEEP. Test it with a stick? Or someone could go in. Feet first. In the dark.

right.label: Yes. Use a stick.
right.reaction: The stick went all the way down. Carl is very excited about it.

left.label: No. I'll go in.
left.reaction: It was deeper than it looked. Much deeper.

cards.text: (The cheese, in a bow tie, wants the first dance. Alone. In the vault. With the door shut. Doug's rule: never be alone with the cheese.) Dance?

right.label: Yes. One dance.
right.reaction: The door closed. The music kept playing.

left.label: No. Group dance.
left.reaction: A group dance. The cheese sat it out. Watching. Humming.

cards.text: Boss. I've made skis. Out of bin lids. I want to ski down the town hall steps. Into the high street. Can I?

right.label: Yes. Ski, Randy.
right.reaction: He reached forty miles an hour. Then the fountain. He's fine. The fountain is not.

left.label: No. Walk down.
left.reaction: He walked down. On the skis. It took two hours.

cards.text: Mayor. Since Randy's ski run, forty raccoons are skiing down City Hall's steps. On bin lids. Ban skiing?

right.label: Yes. Ban it.
right.reaction: Banned. They're sledging now. On Randy. He's fine with it.

left.label: No. Raccoon slalom.
left.reaction: It's an event now. Bad Town Raccoon Slalom. Chad wants to sponsor it.

cards.text: Wooo. Mayor. I'd like to go ice skating. But I go through the ice. Can someone hold my hand? It goes through hands too.

right.label: Yes. I'll hold it.
right.reaction: You held nothing. It was very cold. Wendy said it was the nicest skate she'd had in 135 years.

left.label: No. Watch from the side.
left.reaction: She watched. Through a wall. Sighing. The ice cracked a little out of sympathy.

cards.text: Mr Flaps. Postmaster. My beak has frozen shut. The post is inside. All of it. Thaw me?

right.label: Yes. Gently.
right.reaction: Thawed with a hairdryer. He sneezed four hundred letters. Mostly delivered. Accidentally.

left.label: No. Wait for spring.
left.reaction: The post is in Mr Flaps until spring. He's been registered as a post office.

cards.text: Mayor, Mr Flaps sneezed the council's tax letters into the river. They're frozen in. Like a display. Chip them out?

right.label: Yes. Chip them out.
right.reaction: Chipped out. Readable. Mostly. Everyone owes '£4??'. Doug has rounded up.

left.label: No. Tax amnesty.
left.reaction: Tax amnesty. The happiest day of the year. Doug is in the river. With a chisel.

cards.text: (Gary the vending machine is the warmest thing in town. Forty people are hugging him. He's humming. He seems moved.) Charge for hugs?

right.label: Yes. Hug fee.
right.reaction: 20p a hug. Gary has given every penny back. In crisps. He's that kind of machine.

left.label: No. Free hugs.
left.reaction: Free hugs for everyone. Gary's display reads ':)' all day. His first ever.

cards.text: (Lorraine the seagull has found Sal's frozen chip delivery. All of it. She's skating on it. With friends.) Stop her?

right.label: Yes. Save the chips.
right.reaction: Saved. Sal now has frozen chips. He's selling them as 'ice chips'. They're just ice.

left.label: No. Let them skate.
left.reaction: Forty seagulls skating on chips. Visitors came from the next town to watch.

cards.text: Mayor. Lorraine is back. She's offered to give back the chips. In return for my van. For the winter. Agree?

right.label: Yes. Lend the van.
right.reaction: Lorraine has a van. She's started a chip delivery service. It's faster than Sal's.

left.label: No. Keep the van.
left.reaction: Sal kept the van. Lorraine is sitting on it. All winter. Watching.

cards.text: (Reginald the tortoise has woken up from hibernation. He's on the ice rink. He thinks he's crossing a road. He's very slow on ice.) Help him?

right.label: Yes. Carry him.
right.reaction: Carried across. He's very grateful. He's walking back. To cross it properly.

left.label: No. He'll manage.
left.reaction: He's spinning. Very slowly. The children are calling it 'tortoise ballet'.

cards.text: (Inspector Biscuit has arrested a snowman for loitering. The snowman hasn't moved. Biscuit says this proves it.) Release him?

right.label: Yes. Release him.
right.reaction: Released. He hasn't moved. Biscuit has arrested him again. It's been four times.

left.label: No. The law is the law.
left.reaction: The snowman is in a cell. Melting. Biscuit has filed it as 'escaping'.

cards.text: (Councillor Pebbles has been seen eating the ice sculpture outside City Hall. It was a sculpture of Pebbles.) Commission another?

right.label: Yes. A new one.
right.reaction: A new one. In metal. He's licked it. His tongue's stuck. He looks proud anyway.

left.label: No. One was enough.
left.reaction: No sculpture. He's standing where it was. Very still. Like a sculpture.

cards.text: Mayor, Pebbles's tongue is stuck to the metal sculpture. I can free him with the heat ray. Very low setting. Do it?

right.label: Yes. Low setting.
right.reaction: Freed. The sculpture has a tongue-shaped dent. It's titled 'Pebbles, Licking'.

left.label: No. Warm water.
left.reaction: Warm water worked. He immediately licked it again. Science.

cards.text: Mayor, the Bugle wants to print the paper on snow. It's a trend. People read it in the morning. It melts by lunch. Approve?

right.label: Yes. Snow news.
right.reaction: Snow news is a hit. Nobody can remember bad headlines. You've never been more popular.

left.label: No. Paper stays.
left.reaction: Paper it is. Marge has printed your rejection. In snow. On your car.

cards.text: (Trevor the moth has found the hottest lamp in Bad Town. It's Nora's heat ray. He's on it. He's very happy. He's slightly crispy.) Move him?

right.label: Yes. Move him.
right.reaction: Moved. He went straight back. He says it's love. Nora says it's 400 degrees.

left.label: No. It's love.
left.reaction: He's fine. He's glowing. Nora is writing a paper about him.

cards.text: Dear Mayor. I built a sledge out of the town's old filing cabinet. It goes very fast. The files are still in it. Can I keep it?

right.label: Yes. Sledge on.
right.reaction: He's sledged the whole town's records down Bad Hill. They're very well sorted now. Alphabetically.

left.label: No. Return the files.
left.reaction: Returned. Timmy has built another sledge. Out of Doug's desk. Doug is still at it.

cards.text: Mayor, Timmy's sledge spread the town's records across Bad Hill. They're in the snow. Collect them?

right.label: Yes. Collect them.
right.reaction: Collected. A few are missing. The ones about Randy. Randy is very helpful about it.

left.label: No. Wait for the thaw.
left.reaction: The thaw will reveal them. In order. Linda has a map.

cards.text: Mr Nutkins. The Squirrel Bank's vault has frozen shut. My acorns are in there. Everyone's acorns. I need a loan. A warm one.

right.label: Yes. Lend him heat.
right.reaction: Lent him a radiator. He's charging interest on the warmth. Hourly.

left.label: No. Wait it out.
left.reaction: He's waiting. In a scarf. He's knitted the scarf from acorn shells. It's very uncomfortable.

cards.text: Mayor! Organised snowball fight! Council versus PTA! I'm the referee! Approve it?

right.label: Yes. Snowballs!
right.reaction: The PTA won. Pam threw first. Pam threw hardest. Doug surrendered in a duvet.

left.label: No. Too rough.
left.reaction: Coach is throwing snowballs at himself. To stay in practice.

cards.text: Mayor, the library is the warmest building in town. Everyone's in here. Nobody's reading. Charge for warmth?

right.label: Yes. Warmth fee.
right.reaction: 10p to come in. People are reading now, out of guilt. Linda is delighted.

left.label: No. Free warmth.
left.reaction: Free. Four hundred people. One book. They're taking turns.

cards.text: Mayor, I've strapped my scooter to a sledge. It goes ninety. I'd like to ride down Bad Hill. Permission?

right.label: Yes. Ninety it is.
right.reaction: She hit the bottom at ninety. Kept going. Reached the next town. Waved. Came back for tea.

left.label: No. Forty max.
left.reaction: She did forty. Backwards. On one ski. It was somehow worse.

cards.text: Mayor, I'd like to open a ski resort. On Bad Hill. It's forty feet high. Lift passes are £200. Approve?

right.label: Yes. Chad's Peaks.
right.reaction: One skier. Chad. He reached the bottom in four seconds. He's bought a second hill.

left.label: No. Free sledging.
left.reaction: Free sledging. Chad's skiing on the free hill. Pretending it's his.

cards.text: Boss. I'd like to lend my coat to the homeless shelter. It's very warm. The cousins are coming too. Okay?

right.label: Yes. Lend the coat.
right.reaction: The shelter is very warm. Very full. Mostly raccoons. Everyone's happy.

left.label: No. Keep it.
left.reaction: He's kept it. He's a bit ashamed. He's knitted the shelter a scarf.

cards.text: Mayor. The police car is frozen. I've been patrolling on a tea tray. It's very fast. Buy a new car?

right.label: Yes. New car.
right.reaction: New car. It's frozen too. She's back on the tray. She prefers it.

left.label: No. Tea tray it is.
left.reaction: Tea tray patrol. Arrests are up. Nobody expects the tray.

cards.text: HONK. (Gerald has organised the geese into a formation skating team. They'd like to perform at the Winter Ball.) Book them?

right.label: Yes. Book the geese.
right.reaction: They skated. Then they honked. Then they skated into the cake. Standing ovation.

left.label: No. No geese.
left.reaction: They performed anyway. Outside. In the car park. To one man. He cried.

cards.text: Mayor. It's so cold I can see my breath. It's forming a number. It's the budget deficit. Should I worry?

right.label: Yes. Worry.
right.reaction: He's worrying. Cutting the biscuit budget. Morale has plummeted.

left.label: No. It's just breath.
left.reaction: He's breathing more carefully. The deficit looks smaller. It isn't.

cards.text: Dear Mayor. I built an igloo. It's very good. I'd like it to be a school. Just for me. Can it be?

right.label: Yes. Igloo school.
right.reaction: Professor Hoot has moved in. He's teaching Timmy. At night. In the igloo. It's going very well.

left.label: No. Real school.
left.reaction: He's gone to real school. In the igloo. Carried there by Bev.

cards.text: Stormy Steve. I've forecast a heatwave. In the middle of the freeze. So, more snow. Should I say it out loud?

right.label: Yes. Say it.
right.reaction: 'HEATWAVE,' he said. It snowed for a week. He's so reliably wrong it's comforting.

left.label: No. Keep quiet.
left.reaction: He kept quiet. It was suddenly warm. Everyone blamed him for not saying.

cards.text: Mayor. I'd like to sell fondue. Tyre fondue. You dip a tyre. In cheese. It's warm. Approve the licence?

right.label: Yes. Tyre fondue.
right.reaction: It sold out. The cheese vault hummed with approval. Doug is worried.

left.label: No. Normal fondue.
left.reaction: Normal fondue. Bread only. Sal is dipping the tyres in secret.

cards.text: The PTA would like to run a coat drive. They've collected four hundred coats. All of them are Randy's. They'd like to donate them. Allow it?

right.label: Yes. Donate them.
right.reaction: Donated. Four hundred people in Randy's coats. The cousins are very confused.

left.label: No. Return them.
left.reaction: Returned. Randy is wearing all four hundred. He's spherical.

cards.text: (Clive the traffic cone is completely buried in snow. Only his tip is visible. He seems content.) Dig him out?

right.label: Yes. Dig out Clive.
right.reaction: Dug out. He's facing a different direction. Nobody turned him.

left.label: No. He's resting.
left.reaction: He's still buried. People leave hot drinks by his tip. It's a shrine.

cards.text: Mayor! The Snow App! It tells you when it's snowing! By looking out of the window for you! £4.99! Approve?

right.label: Yes. Launch it.
right.reaction: Four thousand downloads. It says 'yes' every time. It's always right.

left.label: No. Use a window.
left.reaction: Brayden has looked out of the window. He's crying. It's beautiful.

cards.text: (Kevin the pothole has frozen solid. Children are skating on him. Kevin seems delighted. Barb does not.) Allow skating?

right.label: Yes. Skate on Kevin.
right.reaction: The Kevin Rink is open. 50p a go. Kevin has never felt so loved.

left.label: No. Fence him off.
left.reaction: Kevin is fenced off. The children are skating on the fence.

cards.text: Mayor, the Kevin Rink is making more money than the council. Should Kevin get a share? He's a hole.

right.label: Yes. Pay Kevin.
right.reaction: Kevin's share is in a jar. Beside him. Nobody's quite sure what he'll buy.

left.label: No. He's a hole.
left.reaction: The Bugle ran 'MAYOR SHORTCHANGES POTHOLE'. Letters poured in.

cards.text: Dear Mayor. Kevin is lonely behind the fence. I've put a hat on him. Can I take the fence down? Just a bit?

right.label: Yes. A bit.
right.reaction: The fence is down a bit. The whole town came. Kevin's hat blew off. They cheered.

left.label: No. Safety first.
left.reaction: Timmy is sitting next to the fence with Kevin. Holding his hand. Kevin has no hand.

cards.text: (The thaw is coming. Kevin is melting back into a normal pothole. The town has come to say goodbye to the rink.) Make a speech?

right.label: Yes. A speech.
right.reaction: You spoke for ten minutes about a hole. People wept. Kevin gurgled.

left.label: No. It's a pothole.
left.reaction: Chad has filled him with hot chocolate. Selling it by the cup. Kevin seems fine.

cards.text: (Toby the oak tree is cold. He's dropped all his leaves. On your car. On purpose. He'd like a scarf.) Knit him one?

right.label: Yes. A scarf for Toby.
right.reaction: The PTA knitted for a week. It's forty feet long. He's never looked better.

left.label: No. Trees are fine.
left.reaction: Toby is sulking. Branches drooping. A squirrel has taken your side. Only one.

cards.text: Mayor! Toby's scarf is the most photographed thing in town. I'd like to put my logo on it. Small. Very small. Giant.

right.label: Yes. A logo.
right.reaction: 'TOBY: BROUGHT TO YOU BY CHAD'. Toby dropped a branch on Chad. Gently.

left.label: No. It's Toby's.
left.reaction: Chad has knitted his own tree a scarf. It's a lamppost. It's not the same.

cards.text: (Mr Nutkins has noticed Toby is sad. The squirrels would like to move in and keep him warm. All 300.) Allow it?

right.label: Yes. Squirrels in.
right.reaction: Toby is full of squirrels. Very warm. Very loud. He's thrilled.

left.label: No. That's too many.
left.reaction: Mr Nutkins sent 299 squirrels. He says it's a compromise.

cards.text: (Spring is coming. Toby has grown one leaf. Just one. Facing your window. Facing you. It's for you.) Frame it?

right.label: Yes. Frame the leaf.
right.reaction: It's in your office. Toby sways when you walk past. You wave back.

left.label: No. Leave it be.
left.reaction: The Bugle has photographed the leaf. 'TREE LOVES MAYOR?' Everyone's talking.

cards.text: (The Big Freeze has frozen the cheese in the vault. It's quiet for the first time in years. Too quiet.) Warm it up?

right.label: Yes. Warm it up.
right.reaction: A heater in the vault. The cheese thawed. It hummed once. You felt watched.

left.label: No. Peace at last.
left.reaction: The vault is silent. The town sleeps well. Doug keeps checking it. Just in case.

cards.text: Mayor, the cheese has rolled out of the vault and towards the radiator. It's been there all day. Like a cat. Move it?

right.label: Yes. Back in the vault.
right.reaction: It rolled back. It took a while. It felt like a choice.

left.label: No. Let it be warm.
left.reaction: It's purring. Cheese doesn't purr. This one does.

cards.text: Mayor, I scanned the frozen cheese. It's not frozen. It's hibernating. It's dreaming. About you. Should I wake it?

right.label: Yes. Wake it.
right.reaction: It woke up. It hummed your name. The Bugle has a recording. It's number one.

left.label: No. Let it dream.
left.reaction: It's still dreaming. Nora says it's dreaming that it's mayor. It's doing well.

cards.text: (The thaw. The cheese is back to normal. It has left a small wedge of itself on your desk. A gift. Or a warning.) Eat it?

right.label: Yes. Eat the gift.
right.reaction: Delicious. You feel strange. You feel... aged. Gracefully.

left.label: No. Keep it.
left.reaction: It's on your shelf. It doesn't go off. It never will. You can't throw it out.

cards.text: (Inspector Biscuit has found pawprints in the snow leading to the treasury. They're his. He's arrested himself.) Release him?

right.label: Yes. Release Biscuit.
right.reaction: He released himself. With a stern warning. He took it very well.

left.label: No. Justice is justice.
left.reaction: Biscuit is in a cell. He's sad. His tail is wagging anyway.

cards.text: Mayor. New pawprints by the treasury. Not Biscuit's. Bigger. Honk-shaped. Investigate Gerald?

right.label: Yes. Question Gerald.
right.reaction: Gerald was questioned. He honked for an hour. Barb took notes. She now speaks goose.

left.label: No. Leave the geese.
left.reaction: The treasury's bread fund is missing. Four hundred geese look very well fed.

cards.text: Mayor, the Bugle wants to cover the trial of Inspector Biscuit. By Inspector Biscuit. He's also the judge. Allow it?

right.label: Yes. Cover the trial.
right.reaction: Biscuit found himself not guilty. Then gave himself a treat. Sold out.

left.label: No. Keep it quiet.
left.reaction: The Bugle ran 'SECRET DOG TRIAL'. Everyone came. The dog was very good.

cards.text: (Case closed. Inspector Biscuit has solved it. He's brought you the culprit: a single snowball. It's melting.) Convict it?

right.label: Yes. Guilty.
right.reaction: The snowball got life. It got about an hour. Justice was swift. And wet.

left.label: No. Not enough evidence.
left.reaction: The snowball walked free. It rolled, really. Biscuit is watching it. Closely.

objectives.text: Save Mr Frost from the thaw
Give Dennis the penguin a home
Get Business above 65 in the freeze

low:people.title: Snowballed Out
low:people.text: The whole town lined up with snowballs. Bev threw first. Bev threw last. Bev threw most of the middle.

low:business.title: Frozen Out
low:business.text: Every shop shut. Chad moved his business into a glacier. You're the glacier's receptionist now.

low:law.title: Put on Ice
low:law.text: Barb arrested you and kept you in the walk-in freezer. Next to Mr Frost. He was very understanding.

low:press.title: Cold Shoulder
low:press.text: The Bugle stopped mentioning you. Completely. Even when you were on fire. You were not on fire. It's winter.

low:treasury.title: Heating Bill
low:treasury.text: The heating bill came. Doug opened it and lay down in the snow. The town's money is now a snowman.

high:people.title: Carried to the Ball
high:people.text: The town loved you so much they carried you to the Winter Ball. Then kept carrying. You've been at a ball for six weeks.

high:business.title: Franchised
high:business.text: Chad turned you into a franchise. There are forty mayors now. All you. All in different towns. All very tired.

high:law.title: Winter Sheriff
high:law.text: Barb made you Winter Sheriff. You have a badge and a horse. The horse is Gerald. It's going badly.

high:press.title: Front Page, Frozen
high:press.text: The Bugle put you on the front page so often the printing press froze in your shape. Now every page is you.

rare:cheese_mayor.title: The Cheese Is Mayor Now
rare:cheese_mayor.text: You sat behind the cheese. It has been mayor ever since. It has never said a word. It is the most popular mayor in history.

rare:fondue.title: Fondue
rare:fondue.text: You stepped into the fondue. Nobody is quite sure what happened next. There's a statue of you in the square now. It's cheese. It smiles.

trap:thin_ice.title: Through the Ice
trap:thin_ice.text: The sign was about you. You went straight through. Big Carl rescued you. It took four hours. You missed the election.

trap:frost_swap.title: Swapped with a Snowman
trap:frost_swap.text: You stood in the snow all night. Mr Frost sat in your office. By morning he'd been elected and you'd become a snowman.

trap:through_vault.title: The Shortcut
trap:through_vault.text: You took the shortcut through the cheese vault. The cheese let you in. You've been 'in a meeting' ever since.

trap:grit_gift.title: The Grit Incident
trap:grit_gift.text: You accepted Gerald's gift on live television. Nobody will ever look at you the same way again. Approval: grit.

trap:heat_ray.title: Defrosted
trap:heat_ray.text: You pressed the switch on the front. You glow now. Permanently. The town uses you as a streetlight. It's a job.

trap:depth_test.title: Depth Tested
trap:depth_test.text: It was deeper than it looked. Carl rescued you, then himself, then you again. You've retired to a towel.

trap:last_dance.title: Last Dance with the Cheese
trap:last_dance.text: You danced with the cheese in the vault. The door closed. The music kept playing. The cheese leads. It always leads.

outw:people.title: Frozen Out
outw:people.text: The town voted for Mr Frost the snowman. He said nothing all campaign. He was very cool under pressure. Literally.

outw:business.title: Snowed Under
outw:business.text: Every shop was buried. The only business open was Lorraine's chip van, on the church roof. She bought the election with chips.

outw:law.title: Put on Ice
outw:law.text: Barb kept you in the walk-in freezer 'for your own safety'. When the door opened the polls had closed. You were a lolly.

outw:press.title: COLD NEWS
outw:press.text: The Bugle's front page was a photo of you shivering, captioned 'HIM?'. Turnout was huge. All of it was against you.

headlines.trevorlamp: A MOTH ON THE HEAT RAY

cliffhangers: Tomorrow: a snowman wants your job.
Tomorrow: you, Randy, Doug, the Cheese and one sandwich.
Tomorrow: the grit is gone. Gerald is crunchy.
Tomorrow: every pipe in town is frozen.
Tomorrow: Big Carl's pool is ice.
Tomorrow, the last day: the Winter Ball. The Cheese has an invitation.
